data.name: READ THIS FIRST: IMAP, POP3 and SMTP have no way to change a password, and the self-service portal refuses an expired one at sign-in like every other surface. An expired password is therefore renewed by an administrator - or by the person themselves only if they hold an app password, which still signs them in to the portal, where the expired password is accepted as the current one when setting a new one. Turning this on means someone has to be available for everybody else. Existing app passwords keep working, which is also the one way an affected person can still collect mail; Active Directory accounts are exempt, because their password lives in the directory and expires by its policy, not this one. The clock started when this server was upgraded, so nobody is expired the moment you set this.
data.value: LÆS DETTE FØRST: IMAP, POP3 og SMTP har ingen måde at ændre en adgangskode på, og selvbetjeningsportalen afviser en udløbet adgangskode ved logon ligesom enhver anden flade. En udløbet adgangskode fornys derfor af en administrator - eller af personen selv, men kun hvis vedkommende har en app-adgangskode, som stadig logger vedkommende på portalen, hvor den udløbne adgangskode accepteres som den nuværende, når der sættes en ny. At slå dette til betyder, at nogen skal være til rådighed for alle andre. Eksisterende app-adgangskoder bliver ved med at virke, hvilket også er den ene måde, en berørt person stadig kan hente post på; Active Directory-konti er undtaget, fordi deres adgangskode ligger i kataloget og udløber efter dets politik, ikke denne. Uret startede, da denne server blev opgraderet, så ingen er udløbet i det øjeblik, du sætter dette.

data.name: REST listener settings…

RFC 7208 4.6.4. A "void lookup" is a term of a sender's SPF policy - an a:, mx: or exists: - whose DNS query comes back with nothing at all. The separate limit of ten DNS-querying terms bounds what a policy can ask this server to look up; it does not bound what a policy can waste, and ten terms naming hosts that do not exist cost a full resolution each for a record that can never match. Two is what the RFC says. It also catches the ordinary case: a policy still listing hosts decommissioned years ago, which its owner would rather be told about. Raising it is safe; 0 switches the limit off, which is the setting for a correspondent whose policy is wrong in exactly this way and whose mail you would rather take. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: RFC 7208 4.6.4. Et "void lookup" er et led i en afsenders SPF-politik - et a:, mx: eller exists: - hvis DNS-forespørgsel kommer tilbage med slet ingenting. Den særskilte grænse på ti DNS-forespørgende led begrænser, hvad en politik kan bede denne server om at slå op; den begrænser ikke, hvad en politik kan spilde, og ti led, der nævner værter, som ikke findes, koster en fuld opløsning hver for en post, der aldrig kan matche. To er, hvad RFC'en siger. Det fanger også det almindelige tilfælde: en politik, der stadig nævner værter, der blev taget ud af drift for år siden, hvilket dens ejer hellere vil have at vide. At hæve den er sikkert; 0 slår grænsen fra, hvilket er indstillingen for en korrespondent, hvis politik er forkert på nøjagtigt denne måde, og hvis post du hellere vil tage imod. Gælder efter en genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: Received headers

Receivers look up the PTR record of the connecting IP address and compare it with the name the server announces in HELO/EHLO; this server judges incoming mail by the same standard when the PTR and HELO checks on Anti-spam settings are on. Unlike every other record on this page, the PTR is NOT published in your domain's zone: it lives in the reverse zone of the IP address, which belongs to whoever owns the address - usually your hosting provider or ISP. Ask them to set it; there is nothing to paste into your own DNS console.
data.value: Modtagere slår PTR-posten for den forbindende IP-adresse op og sammenligner den med det navn, serveren annoncerer i HELO/EHLO; denne server bedømmer indgående post efter samme målestok, når PTR- og HELO-kontrollerne under Antispam-indstillinger er slået til. I modsætning til hver anden post på denne side offentliggøres PTR-posten IKKE i dit domænes zone: den ligger i IP-adressens omvendte zone, som tilhører den, der ejer adressen - normalt din hostingudbyder eller internetudbyder. Bed dem om at sætte den; der er intet at indsætte i din egen DNS-konsol.

data.name: Required. The Active Directory domain controller or other LDAP server to bind against. For LDAPS the name must match the server's certificate, so use the DNS name, not an IP address.

data.name: Required. With this empty the setting above does nothing at all, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight: anyone can fabricate a whole ARC chain and seal it with a key they publish in their own DNS, and it will validate perfectly, so a passing chain proves nothing unless you already trust the sealer. This list is not an option of the feature - it is the feature. Name the exact domains whose seals you honour (the d= of their ARC-Seal), separated by commas, semicolons or spaces; matching is exact, so a suffix of a trusted name is not trusted.
data.value: Påkrævet. Står dette tomt, gør indstillingen ovenfor slet ingenting, og det er med vilje og ikke en forglemmelse: enhver kan fabrikere en hel ARC-kæde og forsegle den med en nøgle, de offentliggør i deres egen DNS, og den vil validere perfekt, så en kæde, der består, beviser ingenting, medmindre du allerede stoler på forsegleren. Denne liste er ikke en indstilling ved funktionen - den er funktionen. Nævn de nøjagtige domæner, hvis segl du anerkender (d= i deres ARC-Seal), adskilt af kommaer, semikoloner eller mellemrum; matchningen er nøjagtig, så et suffiks af et betroet navn er ikke betroet.

data.name: Runs the same steps the server runs, in the same order, using the values in the editors above as they stand: connect, protect the transport, bind the service credential, search for the user - and, only if a password is typed below, bind as that user to prove it. The password is used once and never stored, and the test refuses to run any configuration that would put a password on the network unprotected. One honest caveat: the test runs from this computer, so a firewall that treats this machine and the hMailServer service differently can make the two disagree.
data.value: Kører de samme trin, som serveren kører, i samme rækkefølge, med værdierne i editorerne ovenfor, som de er nu: forbind, beskyt transporten, bind tjenestens legitimationsoplysninger, søg efter brugeren - og, kun hvis der indtastes en adgangskode nedenfor, bind som den bruger for at bevise det. Adgangskoden bruges én gang og gemmes aldrig, og testen nægter at køre enhver konfiguration, der ville sende en adgangskode ubeskyttet over netværket. Ét ærligt forbehold: testen kører fra denne computer, så en firewall, der behandler denne maskine og hMailServer-tjenesten forskelligt, kan få de to til at være uenige.

data.name: STARTTLS (optional)
STARTTLS (required)

STARTTLS is expected to be offered, using the certificate '{0}' borrowed from a TLS-capable mailbox port - this listener has no certificate setting of its own, by design: the client editing Sieve filters is the client reading the mailbox, so the certificate it already trusts is the right one to present. Whether the files actually load is decided when the service starts; if they do not, the listener runs in plain text and says so in the application log, and the SSL certificates page checks the files themselves.
data.value: STARTTLS forventes at blive tilbudt med certifikatet '{0}', lånt fra en TLS-egnet postkasseport - denne lytter har med vilje ingen egen certifikatindstilling: den klient, der redigerer Sieve-filtre, er den klient, der læser postkassen, så det certifikat, den allerede stoler på, er det rigtige at fremvise. Om filerne rent faktisk indlæses, afgøres, når tjenesten starter; gør de det ikke, kører lytteren i klartekst og siger det i programloggen, og siden SSL-certifikater kontrollerer selve filerne.

data.name: STARTTLS is offered and not required, which is the correct arrangement for port 25: requiring it would refuse mail from senders that cannot offer it.

data.name: STARTTLS is offered but not required. A client that does not ask for it - or one talked out of asking by something in the middle - authenticates in the clear, and neither end is told.

data.name: Sends the daily aggregate reports that domains ask for with a rua= tag in their DMARC record (RFC 7489) - who sent mail claiming to be them, and whether it passed. Reports only go to an address outside the policy domain when that address's own DNS says it wants them, so a domain cannot use its DMARC record to aim this server's reports at somebody else.
data.value: Sender de daglige aggregerede rapporter, som domæner beder om med et rua=-tag i deres DMARC-post (RFC 7489) - hvem der sendte post og påstod at være dem, og om den bestod. Rapporter går kun til en adresse uden for politikdomænet, når den adresses eget DNS siger, at den vil have dem, så et domæne kan ikke bruge sin DMARC-post til at rette denne servers rapporter mod en anden.

data.name: Sends the message as counted chunks rather than dot-stuffed DATA. It is also what carries a binary message onward without rewriting it: a message accepted as BINARYMIME can only be relayed as it arrived to a server that offers both this and BINARYMIME. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: Sender meddelelsen som optalte bidder frem for som DATA med dot-stuffing. Det er også det, der bærer en binær meddelelse videre uden at omskrive den: en meddelelse, der er accepteret som BINARYMIME, kan kun relayes, som den ankom, til en server, der tilbyder både dette og BINARYMIME. Gælder efter en genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: Sends the recipient's address as the User: header, so spamd applies that mailbox's own preferences - the shape a virtual-user spamd (--virtual-config-dir with %u or %d) expects. A scan runs once per message, not once per recipient, so a message to several people cannot be scanned under any one of their preferences and uses the profile above instead.

En scanning kører én gang pr. meddelelse, ikke én gang pr. modtager, så en meddelelse til flere personer kan ikke scannes under nogen af deres præferencer og bruger profilen ovenfor i stedet.

data.name: Simple is the default. Negotiate runs an SSPI exchange (Kerberos, falling back to NTLM) that never transmits the password and signs the connection - it is the only method a default-configured modern domain controller accepts when it has no certificate installed, it needs no search, no SearchBase and no service account, and it works from a host that is not domain-joined.
data.value: Simple er standarden. Negotiate kører en SSPI-udveksling (Kerberos, med fallback til NTLM), der aldrig sender adgangskoden og signerer forbindelsen - det er den eneste metode, en moderne domænecontroller med standardkonfiguration accepterer, når den ikke har noget certifikat installeret, den har ikke brug for søgning, SearchBase eller tjenestekonto, og den virker fra en vært, der ikke er tilsluttet et domæne.

data.name: Size limit and scanners…
Skipped, by reason

Slows a session that names more recipients than a legitimate message needs. Past the count, every further RCPT TO in an unauthenticated session waits the delay before it is answered - a dictionary attack or a spam run names hundreds of addresses and pays for each one, while a sending MTA names a handful and never reaches the count. Authenticated sessions and IP ranges with spam protection off are exempt. The wait is a timer on the connection, not a thread asleep. Takes effect at once; stored in hMailServer.ini as SmtpTarpitCount and SmtpTarpitDelaySeconds.
data.value: Bremser en session, der nævner flere modtagere, end en legitim meddelelse har brug for. Over antallet venter hver yderligere RCPT TO i en ugodkendt session på forsinkelsen, før den besvares - et ordbogsangreb eller en spamkørsel nævner hundredvis af adresser og betaler for hver enkelt, mens en afsendende MTA nævner en håndfuld og aldrig når antallet. Godkendte sessioner og IP-intervaller med spambeskyttelse slået fra er undtaget. Ventetiden er en timer på forbindelsen, ikke en sovende tråd. Får virkning med det samme; gemmes i hMailServer.ini som SmtpTarpitCount og SmtpTarpitDelaySeconds.

data.name: TLS 1.3
TLS 1.3 cipher suites (empty = OpenSSL defaults)

TLS 1.3 has its own suite list, its own names and its own setter, so the cipher list above does not restrict it. Colon separated, most preferred first, using the RFC 8446 names (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256) - not the OpenSSL cipher-list names. Leave empty to keep OpenSSL's defaults; a name this build does not recognise is skipped and reported rather than failing the whole list.

Kolonsepareret, mest foretrukne først, med RFC 8446-navnene (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256) - ikke OpenSSL's cipher-listenavne. Lad stå tomt for at beholde OpenSSL's standarder; et navn, denne build ikke genkender, springes over og rapporteres i stedet for at få hele listen til at fejle.

data.name: The counterpart to ARC sealing: on inbound mail, a valid ARC chain from a trusted sealer can offset the DMARC failure score for a message whose DMARC pass was destroyed by forwarding (RFC 8617). It is configured on the Anti-spam page, under sender authentication, because it is stored with the other anti-spam settings rather than in hMailServer.INI. With the trusted-sealer list empty the feature does nothing at all, by design: anyone can fabricate an entire ARC chain and seal it with keys published in their own DNS, and it will validate perfectly, so a passing chain proves nothing unless you already trust the sealer. The list is not an option of the feature - it is the feature. The offset never exceeds the DMARC failure score, and applies only while DMARC scoring is enabled on the Anti-spam page.
data.value: Modstykket til ARC-forsegling: på indgående post kan en gyldig ARC-kæde fra en betroet forsegler opveje DMARC-fejlscoren for en meddelelse, hvis DMARC-godkendelse blev ødelagt af videresendelse (RFC 8617). Det konfigureres på siden Antispam-indstillinger under afsendergodkendelse, fordi det gemmes sammen med de andre antispam-indstillinger og ikke i hMailServer.INI. Med en tom liste over betroede forseglere gør funktionen slet ingenting, og det er med vilje: enhver kan fabrikere en hel ARC-kæde og forsegle den med nøgler publiceret i sit eget DNS, og den vil validere perfekt, så en godkendt kæde beviser intet, medmindre du allerede stoler på forsegleren. Listen er ikke en mulighed i funktionen - den er funktionen. Opvejningen overstiger aldrig DMARC-fejlscoren og gælder kun, mens DMARC-scoring er aktiveret på siden Antispam-indstillinger.

data.name: The delivery that takes a mailbox past this percentage produces one notice to the person whose mailbox it is, from their own domain's postmaster. ONE, not one per message: the server treats the threshold as something the mailbox CROSSES rather than a state it is in, so a mailbox sitting at 95% is not warned about again on every delivery - which would fill it faster than the mail does. Emptying the mailbox and filling it again warns again, which is the behaviour anyone would expect and is free here rather than something that had to be remembered and expired. On by default, because the alternative is what this server did before: say nothing at all until mail starts being refused, by which point the person it happens to is the last to know. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: Den levering, der bringer en postkasse forbi denne procent, giver én besked til den person, hvis postkasse det er, fra dennes eget domænes postmaster. ÉN, ikke én pr. meddelelse: serveren behandler tærsklen som noget, postkassen KRYDSER, snarere end en tilstand, den er i, så en postkasse, der står på 95 %, advares ikke igen ved hver levering - hvilket ville fylde den hurtigere, end posten gør. Tømmes postkassen og fyldes igen, advares der igen, hvilket er den adfærd, enhver ville forvente, og her er den gratis i stedet for noget, der skulle huskes og udløbe. Slået til som standard, fordi alternativet er, hvad denne server gjorde før: sige ingenting overhovedet, indtil post begynder at blive afvist, og på det tidspunkt er den, det sker for, den sidste, der ved det. Gælder efter genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: The group members could not be read:

The groups this server will agree a TLS key with, in OpenSSL's list form. As shipped it offers the two post-quantum hybrids first and falls back to X25519 and the NIST curves for a peer that has neither, so nothing changes for an older client. An empty list, or one OpenSSL rejects or that would leave no group enabled, is not applied: the server logs it and uses the classical fallback, so a mistake here cannot take TLS down - but it does silently give up the hybrids, which is why the shipped list is shown rather than a blank. Change it against a scan rather than in the dark. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: De grupper, som denne server vil aftale en TLS-nøgle med, i OpenSSLs listeform. Som leveret tilbyder den de to postkvante-hybrider først og falder tilbage til X25519 og NIST-kurverne for en modpart, der ikke har nogen af dem, så intet ændrer sig for en ældre klient. En tom liste, eller en som OpenSSL afviser, eller som ikke ville lade nogen gruppe være aktiveret, anvendes ikke: serveren logger den og bruger det klassiske fallback, så en fejl her kan ikke tage TLS ned - men den opgiver stille hybriderne, og derfor vises den leverede liste frem for et tomt felt. Ændr den op imod en scanning frem for i blinde. Gælder efter en genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: The hMailServer 6.x line is one such effort. The original open-source mail server has been rebuilt on a current toolchain (Visual Studio 2026 / MSVC v145 and .NET 10), re-armed with modern cryptography (PBKDF2 / Argon2id, SCRAM-SHA-256, OAuth2) and the transport-security standards expected of a mail server today (DANE + DNSSEC, MTA-STS, ARC, Ed25519 DKIM, TLS-RPT and ACME / Let's Encrypt). It has been hardened against protocol and denial-of-service defects, given Sieve / ManageSieve filtering, health and OpenTelemetry observability, broad MySQL / MariaDB / MS SQL / PostgreSQL support, and this modern Fluent-design Control Panel in place of the legacy administrator.
data.value: hMailServer 6.x-serien er en sådan indsats. Den oprindelige open source-postserver er genopbygget på en aktuel værktøjskæde (Visual Studio 2026 / MSVC v145 og .NET 10), genudstyret med moderne kryptografi (PBKDF2 / Argon2id, SCRAM-SHA-256, OAuth2) og de transportsikkerhedsstandarder, der forventes af en postserver i dag (DANE + DNSSEC, MTA-STS, ARC, Ed25519 DKIM, TLS-RPT og ACME / Let's Encrypt). Den er hærdet mod protokol- og denial-of-service-fejl, har fået Sieve / ManageSieve-filtrering, sundheds- og OpenTelemetry-observabilitet, bred MySQL / MariaDB / MS SQL / PostgreSQL-understøttelse og dette moderne Control Panel i Fluent-design i stedet for den gamle administrator.

The last five settings on this card are for a site that builds its own releases and signs them with its own Sigstore, or that mirrors this project's. Leave every one of them empty and the server trusts exactly one thing: an installer signed by this project's own release workflow, recorded in the public transparency log. Setting any of them narrows or replaces that, and getting one wrong means either refusing genuine releases or trusting somebody else's.

Lad hver eneste af dem være tom, så stoler serveren på præcis én ting: et installationsprogram signeret af dette projekts egen udgivelsesarbejdsgang, registreret i den offentlige gennemsigtighedslog. At sætte en af dem indsnævrer eller erstatter det, og at få en af dem forkert betyder enten at afvise ægte udgivelser eller at stole på en andens.

data.name: The server state could not be changed: {0}

The server stores this value and never reads it - nothing sets a thread priority from it, so changing it has no effect. It is shown rather than removed so that an administrator who set it years ago can see it is still there and why nothing happened, and it is not editable because a box that accepts a value nothing acts on is worse than no box at all. The thread counts above are honoured.

data.name: The single value AEAD-ONLY (case-insensitive) is a named preset rather than an OpenSSL cipher string: forward-secret AEAD suites only (ECDHE or DHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305), excluding every CBC-mode suite - the Lucky13 padding-oracle family - and static-RSA key exchange. The cost: TLS 1.2 clients that only speak CBC suites cannot connect, and TLS 1.0/1.1 are left with no usable cipher at all, so do not enable those protocols alongside it. TLS 1.3 is unaffected - its suites are AEAD by construction and are configured separately below. A misspelled preset name is rejected and reported, not silently ignored.
data.value: Den enkeltstående værdi AEAD-ONLY (uden forskel på store og små bogstaver) er en navngivet forudindstilling snarere end en OpenSSL-cipher-streng: kun forward-secret AEAD-suiter (ECDHE eller DHE med AES-GCM eller ChaCha20-Poly1305), med udelukkelse af alle suiter i CBC-tilstand - Lucky13-familien af padding-oracle-angreb - og statisk RSA-nøgleudveksling. Prisen: TLS 1.2-klienter, der kun taler CBC-suiter, kan ikke forbinde, og TLS 1.0/1.1 står tilbage uden nogen brugbar cipher overhovedet, så aktivér ikke de protokoller sammen med den. TLS 1.3 påvirkes ikke - dens suiter er AEAD af konstruktion og konfigureres separat nedenfor. Et forkert stavet forudindstillingsnavn afvises og rapporteres, ikke ignoreres stille.

data.name: These belong together: expiry without history teaches people to alternate between two passwords, which is worse than not expiring at all. History only ever refuses a CHANGE, at the moment somebody is able to pick something else, so nobody is locked out by it. Expiry refuses a LOGON - read its description before turning it on.

Historikken afviser kun en ÆNDRING, i det øjeblik nogen kan vælge noget andet, så ingen låses ude af den. Udløb afviser en PÅLOGNING - læs dets beskrivelse, før du slår det til.

data.name: This is [Settings] UseLanguage in hMailServer.INI. The server only hands it back over the COM API - it does not translate anything itself, and this Control Panel has a language setting of its own (the globe button in the sidebar) - so it affects third-party administration tools only. Bounce and error wording is on the Server messages page.

Serveren giver den kun tilbage over COM API'et - den oversætter ikke selv noget, og dette Control Panel har sin egen sprogindstilling (globusknappen i sidepanelet) - så den påvirker kun tredjeparts administrationsværktøjer. Ordlyden af afvisninger og fejl er på siden Servermeddelelser.

data.name: This is the latest release
This is the only time it will ever be shown. The store keeps a SHA-256 digest, not the key, so it cannot be recovered or re-displayed - if it is lost, revoke it here and create another.

data.name: This key file is encrypted (passphrase-protected). Enter its passphrase in the box below before adding, or the key will not load (server error 6170) and the TLS ports using this certificate will not start.

data.name: This page used to collect every hMailServer.INI value without a home, which meant it was filed by where the value is stored rather than by what it does - and where a value is stored is the one thing you never need to know. Each of these now sits with the rest of its own feature. Nothing was removed and no value changed; only the page it is edited on.
data.value: Denne side samlede tidligere enhver hMailServer.INI-værdi uden et hjem, hvilket betød, at den blev sorteret efter, hvor værdien gemmes, i stedet for efter, hvad den gør - og hvor en værdi gemmes, er det ene, du aldrig behøver at vide. Hver af dem sidder nu sammen med resten af sin egen funktion. Intet blev fjernet, og ingen værdi ændrede sig; kun den side, den redigeres på.

data.name: This panel can compare RSA and ECDSA keys; this key parses as neither, so whether it matches the certificate is only proven when the server loads the pair.

data.name: This range _expires

This runs before virus scanning and independently of it: it applies even with every scanner switched off, and it applies to messages the size limit above would skip. A matched attachment is replaced by a short text file explaining the removal rather than being deleted outright, so the recipient can tell something was taken out.
data.value: Dette kører før virusscanning og uafhængigt af den: det gælder, selv med alle scannere slået fra, og det gælder for meddelelser, som størrelsesgrænsen ovenfor ville springe over. En matchet vedhæftet fil erstattes med en kort tekstfil, der forklarer fjernelsen, i stedet for at blive slettet direkte, så modtageren kan se, at noget blev taget ud.

data.name: This runs while the sending server waits for its answer to DATA, so the number is a promise about the worst case rather than a hint. It bounds the connection as well as the reply: an engine whose machine has gone away would otherwise cost the operating system's own TCP timeout on every message.
data.value: Dette kører, mens den afsendende server venter på sit svar på DATA, så tallet er et løfte om det værste tilfælde snarere end et vink. Det begrænser forbindelsen såvel som svaret: en motor, hvis maskine er forsvundet, ville ellers koste operativsystemets egen TCP-timeout på hver meddelelse.

data.name: This server only CHECKS SPF on incoming mail; publishing the record is for everyone else - it tells receiving servers which machines are allowed to send mail claiming to be from

data.name: This setting lives on each IP range rather than with the rest of TLS, which is the main reason it goes unnoticed. It is the only control that refuses a plaintext password regardless of what the port allows, so it is what makes an optional-STARTTLS port safe for clients.
data.value: Denne indstilling bor på hvert IP-interval i stedet for sammen med resten af TLS, hvilket er hovedårsagen til, at den overses. Den er den eneste kontrol, der afviser en klartekst-adgangskode uanset, hvad porten tillader, så det er den, der gør en port med valgfri STARTTLS sikker for klienter.

Tilføj de afsendere til posten først.

data.name: Three things have to be true of that account before the service will start under it, and none of them can be done from here. It needs the "Log on as a service" right (secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment, or your domain policy). It needs full control of the data folder, the log folder and - for the built-in database - the database folder, plus read access to the program folder AND write access to hMailServer.INI inside it, because the service writes its own settings there; if that file is read-only to the account, saved settings are lost at the next restart with no error. And for an external database it needs whatever that server requires, which for MSSQL with integrated security means a login of its own. A service that cannot log on reports error 1069 in the Windows event log and does not start.
data.value: Tre ting skal være sande for den konto, før tjenesten starter under den, og ingen af dem kan gøres herfra. Den skal have rettigheden "Log på som en tjeneste" (secpol.msc > Lokale politikker > Tildeling af brugerrettigheder eller din domænepolitik). Den skal have fuld kontrol over datamappen, logmappen og - for den indbyggede database - databasemappen, plus læseadgang til programmappen OG skriveadgang til hMailServer.INI inde i den, fordi tjenesten skriver sine egne indstillinger dér; er den fil skrivebeskyttet for kontoen, går gemte indstillinger tabt ved næste genstart uden nogen fejl. Og for en ekstern database skal den have, hvad den server kræver, hvilket for MSSQL med integreret sikkerhed betyder et login af sin egen. En tjeneste, der ikke kan logge på, rapporterer fejl 1069 i Windows' hændelseslog og starter ikke.

Any token your identity provider signs with this key is accepted - including one it issued to a different application entirely, which is enough to log in as whichever mailbox that token names. Set both to the exact values your provider puts in its tokens.

data.name: Turning this off stops session tickets on every TLS version: TLS 1.2 and older clients fall back to the server-side session cache, which never leaves this process, and TLS 1.3 clients are sent no ticket at all. For an administrator whose policy is that nothing derived from a long-lived key ever goes on the wire. The only cost is resumption efficiency - every client can still connect with a full handshake.

For en administrator, hvis politik er, at intet afledt af en langlivet nøgle nogensinde går over ledningen. Den eneste omkostning er effektiviteten ved genoptagelse - enhver klient kan stadig forbinde med et fuldt handshake.

data.name: Two bind methods, and the difference matters more than it looks: one sends the password to the directory, the other never puts it on the wire at all.

data.name: Two halves: a TXT record that tells senders a policy exists, and the policy itself, fetched from https://mta-sts.{0}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. This server serves that policy itself - there is no file to upload - when MtaStsHostingEnabled is on and an HTTPS web-services listener is running (RFC 8461 section 3.3 allows HTTPS only). The name mta-sts.{0} also needs an A or CNAME record pointing at this server, and the listener's certificate must cover that name.
data.value: To halvdele: en TXT-post, der fortæller afsendere, at en politik findes, og selve politikken, hentet fra https://mta-sts.{0}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. Denne server serverer selv den politik - der er ingen fil at uploade - når MtaStsHostingEnabled er slået til, og en HTTPS-lytter for webtjenester kører (RFC 8461 afsnit 3.3 tillader kun HTTPS). Navnet mta-sts.{0} skal også have en A- eller CNAME-post, der peger på denne server, og lytterens certifikat skal dække det navn.

data.name: What it may do

What rotation defends: OpenSSL's default ticket key is generated once, when the listener starts, and is never rotated, so every ticket that listener issues for the life of the process is sealed under the same key - and that key, recovered later, decrypts every ticket ever recorded. With an interval set, a captured ticket is useless after at most two intervals. 86400 is a day. Only meaningful while session tickets are enabled above.
data.value: Hvad rotation forsvarer mod: OpenSSL's standard-ticketnøgle genereres én gang, når lytteren starter, og roteres aldrig, så hver ticket, den lytter udsteder i hele processens levetid, forsegles under den samme nøgle - og den nøgle, gendannet senere, dekrypterer hver ticket, der nogensinde er optaget. Med et interval sat er en opsnappet ticket ubrugelig efter højst to intervaller. 86400 er en dag. Kun meningsfuldt, mens session tickets er aktiveret ovenfor.

data.name: What stops one statement blocked on a lock from holding a worker thread for ever. Honoured at connect time by MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL; MS SQL and SQL CE start at ADO's own 30 seconds and pick this value up on any connection that has run an upgrade or maintenance script. Those scripts run under a 30-minute per-statement ceiling of their own regardless of this value. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: Hvad der forhindrer én sætning, der er blokeret på en lås, i at holde en arbejdstråd for evigt. Respekteres ved forbindelse af MySQL/MariaDB og PostgreSQL; MS SQL og SQL CE starter på ADO's egne 30 sekunder og samler denne værdi op på enhver forbindelse, der har kørt et opgraderings- eller vedligeholdelsesscript. Disse scripts kører under deres eget loft på 30 minutter pr. sætning uanset denne værdi. Gælder efter genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: What the server does as the message-store volume fills. Both values are absolute megabytes rather than percentages, because what decides whether the next message fits is how many bytes are left, not what fraction of the volume they are. Applies after a service restart.

Begge værdier er absolutte megabyte snarere end procenter, fordi det, der afgør, om der er plads til den næste meddelelse, er, hvor mange bytes der er tilbage, ikke hvilken brøkdel af volumenet de er. Gælder efter genstart af tjenesten.

data.name: Which Windows account the hMailServer service logs on as. By default that is LocalSystem - the most privileged account on the machine - so a flaw reachable through SMTP, IMAP or POP3 is reachable with full control of the computer. Running the service as a dedicated account is the single largest reduction in what a compromise is worth, and the recommended one is the password-less virtual account NT SERVICE\hMailServer.

Som standard er det LocalSystem - den mest privilegerede konto på maskinen - så en fejl, der kan nås gennem SMTP, IMAP eller POP3, kan nås med fuld kontrol over computeren. At køre tjenesten som en dedikeret konto er den enkeltstående største reduktion af, hvad en kompromittering er værd, og den anbefalede er den adgangskodeløse virtuelle konto NT SERVICE\hMailServer.

List the addresses you administer from under never-ban first.

data.name: With this on, MAIL FROM in an authenticated session must be the account's own address, an alias that resolves to it, or another mailbox whose owner has granted the account the post (p) right on their INBOX - which is how Send-As for a shared mailbox is granted, from any IMAP client's ACL editor (SETACL) or over the COM API. Anything else is refused with 550 5.7.1 before a byte of the message is accepted, so one compromised or careless account can no longer send as every other. Off by default because nothing constrained this before and an installation may depend on that; the null sender is always allowed. Unauthenticated sessions are unaffected. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: Med dette slået til skal MAIL FROM i en godkendt session være kontoens egen adresse, et alias, der slår op til den, eller en anden postkasse, hvis ejer har givet kontoen rettigheden post (p) på sin INBOX - hvilket er, hvordan Send som for en delt postkasse tildeles, fra enhver IMAP-klients ACL-editor (SETACL) eller over COM API'et. Alt andet afvises med 550 5.7.1, før en byte af meddelelsen accepteres, så én kompromitteret eller skødesløs konto ikke længere kan sende som alle andre. Slået fra som standard, fordi intet begrænsede dette før, og en installation kan afhænge af det; null-afsenderen er altid tilladt. Ugodkendte sessioner påvirkes ikke. Gælder efter genstart af tjenesten.

Write-only: a stored password is never shown here again - leave the box blank to keep it. Den forlader kun nogensinde serveren over den transport, der er konfigureret ovenfor.

data.name: Writes the conditions an operator alerts on - database unavailable, a listener that would not start, a crash, a failed backup, the disk floor - to the Windows Application log, where Event Viewer, monitoring agents and SIEM collectors can see them. Stable event ids (the table lives in WindowsEventLog.h); a healthy server writes nothing at all. Protocol traffic and routine logging never go here - a mail server that logs every session to the Application log gets itself uninstalled.

Stabile hændelses-id'er (tabellen ligger i WindowsEventLog.h); en sund server skriver slet ingenting. Protokoltrafik og rutinemæssig logføring havner aldrig her - en mailserver, der logger hver session til programloggen, får sig selv afinstalleret.

data.name: hMailServer does NOT implement CalDAV or CardDAV. These settings only answer the well-known discovery URLs (RFC 6764) with a redirect to the server that does, so a client configured with a user's mail address finds their calendar without being told a second address. Leave both empty unless you run such a server: empty means the discovery URLs answer 404, which is the honest response when there is nothing to point at. They need the web services listener above to be running, like everything else on this page.
data.value: hMailServer implementerer IKKE CalDAV eller CardDAV. Disse indstillinger besvarer kun de velkendte discovery-URL'er (RFC 6764) med en omdirigering til den server, der gør, så en klient, der er sat op med en brugers mailadresse, finder deres kalender uden at få oplyst endnu en adresse. Lad begge stå tomme, medmindre du driver sådan en server: tomt betyder, at discovery-URL'erne svarer 404, hvilket er det ærlige svar, når der ikke er noget at pege på. De kræver, at webtjenestelytteren ovenfor kører, ligesom alt andet på denne side.

data.name: hMailServer does not create or manage client certificates. The certificate authority and the client certificates themselves must be produced outside hMailServer (for example with OpenSSL or an internal PKI) - the server only trusts the CA bundle it is given here.

data.name: hMailServer.ini setting BackupMessagesDBOnly. The backup then records which messages exist but not their contents, and a restore expects the files to still be in the data folder. Applies to backup and restore, after a service restart.

data.name: hMailServer.ini setting BackupVerifyRestore, on by default. After the archive is written its message store is extracted to the temp folder through the same code a restore uses, held to exactly the files the backup staged, and every message row is checked for its file; the result is in the backup log. The store exists twice while it runs, so turn it off for a store the temp volume cannot hold. Applies after a service restart.
data.value: hMailServer.ini-indstillingen BackupVerifyRestore, slået til som standard. Når arkivet er skrevet, udpakkes dets meddelelseslager til temp-mappen gennem den samme kode, som en gendannelse bruger, holdt til nøjagtigt de filer, sikkerhedskopien klargjorde, og hver meddelelsesrække kontrolleres for sin fil; resultatet står i sikkerhedskopieringsloggen. Lageret findes to gange, mens det kører, så slå det fra for et lager, som temp-volumen ikke kan rumme. Gælder efter en genstart af tjenesten.

p=none is the right starting point, not an oversight: it makes receivers check and report but deliver as normal. A stricter policy (quarantine or reject) tells every receiver to junk or refuse mail that fails alignment - and until reports show your own mail passing SPF or DKIM, the mail that fails will include yours. Tighten only after the reports say it is safe.
data.value: p=none er det rigtige udgangspunkt, ikke en forglemmelse: det får modtagere til at kontrollere og rapportere, men levere som normalt. En strengere politik (quarantine eller reject) fortæller hver modtager, at post, der ikke består alignment, skal smides i spam eller afvises - og indtil rapporterne viser, at din egen post består SPF eller DKIM, vil den post, der fejler, omfatte din. Stram først, når rapporterne siger, at det er sikkert.
